t: Royal Prussia was formed when the Prussian Confederation of nobles and burghers rose against the Teutonic Order in 1454 and the Thirteen Years' War ended with the Second Peace of Thorn in 1466.
Until 1569 it kept its own laws, council and parliament, and only Prussians could hold its offices under the ius indigenatus.
The Union of Lublin of 1569 integrated it fully into the Kingdom of Poland, and the partitions of 1772 and 1793 gave its lands to the Kingdom of Prussia.
dyk: Before the Union of Lublin, the Polish chancellor openly admitted that integrating Royal Prussia breached the law by violating the privileges granted in 1454.
ev: Nobles and cities found the Prussian Confederation at Marienwerder against the Teutonic Order's policies
King Casimir IV Jagiellon issues the Incorporation Act, and the Thirteen Years' War begins
The Second Peace of Thorn cedes Pomerelia and western Prussia to the Polish Crown
After the priests' war, Warmia is formally incorporated into Poland
The Statute of Prussia brings many Polish legal solutions into the Prussian legal system
Sejmiks are established and the Prussian parliament takes its bicameral form; Protestantism becomes the ruling religion in Danzig, Elbing and Thorn
The Union of Lublin integrates Royal Prussia fully into the Kingdom of Poland
In the first partition of Poland the Kingdom of Prussia annexes most of the former Royal Prussia

f.capital: No single capital; the great cities Danzig (Gdańsk), Thorn (Toruń) and Elbing (Elbląg) led the province
f.founder: Created by the Second Peace of Thorn (1466) after the Prussian Confederation's revolt against the Teutonic Order
f.successor: Kingdom of Prussia (province of West Prussia)
